items.title: Euro futures test May highs ahead of Jackson Hole symposium.
items.excerpt: Euro futures tested their highest levels since mid-May before reversing course to close near unchanged at 1.1675. The currency rallied as news of increased bond buybacks from the Treasury pushed the U.S. dollar to three-month lows. In the options market, the CVOL index showed volatility easing slightly as prices backed off their daily highs. Traders now turn their attention to Friday's S P Global PMI data, with a broader market focus shifting to next week's highly anticipated central bank meetings at the Jackson Hole Symposium.

items.title: Retail earnings highlight selective consumers.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the morning's market action, noting early losses in equities with Russell futures leading the decline. He covers the slight upward correction in Treasury yields and a modestly stronger U.S. dollar, alongside mixed metals and Bitcoin climbing back above the 71,000 level. Bob dives deep into this week's heavy slate of retail earnings from names like Home Depot, Lowe's, Target, and Walmart, which point to a resilient but highly selective consumer prioritizing value and necessities. He also explains why tomorrow's manufacturing PMI remains a critical cyclical indicator for traders despite its smaller share of the U.S. economy. Finally, he previews upcoming earnings and global economic data including Japan's CPI and U.K. retail sales.

items.excerpt: Key Points: Treasury s decision to double long-end bond buybacks sent a powerful signal : The amounts remain small, but the market reaction suggests investors see an increasing willingness to prevent disorderly rises in long-term borrowing costs. Precious metals, led by gold may benefit whether long yields fall or fiscal concerns eventually push them higher : Lower yields reduce gold s opportunity cost, while higher term premiums driven by fiscal credibility concerns may reinforce demand for hard assets. Dollar weakness adds another important layer of support : If greater official intervention in Treasury markets is interpreted as facilitating easier financial conditions, diversification away from dollar assets could provide an additional tailwind for precious metals. items.title: The FX Trader: US dollar plunges on Bessent’s intervention
items.excerpt: Small amounts but a loud signal from the US treasury The latest US Treasury announces doubling and moving forward of its Treasury buyback operations. The amounts in question in this announcement are a mere pittance an added USD 2 billion (to USD 4 billion total) in purchases of longer-term treasuries of 10 or more years to maturity. The buybacks will start September 9, a hint that the Treasury didn t feel it could wait until the regularly scheduled November 4 meeting, which will see further details. While the amounts are tiny, the signal value is loud indeed as it shows the Treasury does not want higher yields, at least not at the longer end of the yield curve. The move is a shot across the bow against speculating against US treasuries, while offering perhaps some solace for longer term…

items.title: Japanese Yen futures jump ahead of national CPI report.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the recent price action in Japanese Yen futures, highlighting a recovery after six lower closes in the last seven sessions. The yen found support from the U.S. Treasury's announcement to double the size of its long-dated buybacks, increasing operations in the 10- to 30-year part of the curve to at least 4 billion. Looking ahead, Iaccino previews Japan's upcoming national CPI report, noting that June core inflation remained below the Bank of Japan's 2% target and exploring how tomorrow's numbers could influence future central bank policy and currency direction.

items.title: Treasury doubles bond buybacks.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down the morning market action, noting an early lift in stocks led by Russell 2000 futures. The spotlight shifts to the U.S. Treasury, which announced it will double the size of its long bond buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation. Bob explains how this impacts long-end yields and supports risk assets. Traders also look ahead to today's FOMC minutes release at 2:00 PM EDT for a clearer view of the recent committee rate split. Finally, he outlines the heavy schedule ahead, highlighting key corporate earnings, the PBOC rate decision, and upcoming U.S. economic data including jobless claims and the Philly Fed manufacturing index.

items.title: Calm crude, tightening diesel: the real oil market stress is downstream
items.excerpt: Key Points: Hormuz remains severely impaired : US-Iran negotiations remain deadlocked and tanker traffic through the Strait has slowed again, leaving Middle Eastern exports well below normal despite numerous efforts to reroute supply. Crude prices understate the disruption : Alternative pipelines, strategic stock releases, weak Chinese demand and demand destruction have prevented a much larger crude rally, with Brent holding around USD 90 despite the prolonged disruption. Diesel reveals the real stress: Disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian refined-product supply have pushed the WTI-ULSD and Brent-gasoil cracks to record levels around USD 103 and USD 77 per barrel respectively. Borrowing oil from the future has limits : Strategic reserves have helped bridge the supply gap, but…

items.excerpt: Key takeaways Humanoids are the headline, but robotics already spans factories, warehouses, vision systems, motion control and artificial intelligence. items.title: Australian Dollar futures pull back from 2.5-month high as commodities decline.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming discusses the Australian Dollar pulling back from a 2.5-month high, dropping 0.25% to trade around 0.7085. He highlights how slight U.S. dollar strength and selling pressure across commodity markets—particularly in copper, gold, and silver—are influencing the Aussie. Despite short-term hesitation and broad FX weakness hitting the New Zealand and Australian dollars hardest, Deming notes the general uptrend since June remains intact.

items.title: Markets React to Geopolitical Tensions and Fed Outlook.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners recaps the morning's market action as U.S. equities open lower, led by a drop in Nasdaq futures. He covers rising diesel prices tied to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and breaks down the latest global economic data, including UK jobs and Eurozone sentiment. Domestically, U.S. housing starts are in focus alongside declining precious metals and climbing U.S. Treasury yields. Iaccino also examines the CME FedWatch Tool's shifting probabilities for a September rate hike ahead of critical FOMC minutes, wrapping up with a look at upcoming major retail earnings from Target, Lowe's, and TJX.

items.title: Copper versus gold: what an old macro signal is telling us now
items.excerpt: Key Points: Copper-to-gold ratio remains historically low : Around 3.24, still signaling gold s strength, though copper has recently recovered slightly. Macro signal is less clear : Copper reflects industrial demand, but electrification, AI buildout, supply constraints, and geopolitics now play a larger role; gold is supported by central bank buying and diversification. Copper is still an industrial meta l: Higher prices can trigger substitution, efficiency gains, and demand destruction. Gold faces fewer constraints : Driven by investment and central banks, it is less exposed to demand destruction and may outperform in a risk-hedging environment. items.title: British Pound futures hit 3-month high on UK GDP data.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down price action in British Pound futures as the September contract reached a three-month high before settling higher for the session. UK second-quarter GDP data met expectations with 0.4% growth, while June output rose 0.3%, offering support to hawkish Bank of England policymakers. With no BOE meeting scheduled until September 17, foreign exchange markets remain attuned to U.S. inflation and labor data as key drivers for currency valuation.
